extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of art, architecture, and moral aesthetics (art historians and critics)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-aesthetic guidance on how Renaissance art, education, and imagination should be evaluated and what constitutes moral or artistic decline; oriented toward judging architecture, painting, and cultural education. Extracts normative claims about form vs. substance, imagination's purpose, technique vs. subject, and the grotesque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of substance over form
rubrics_metrics.description: “It acted first, as before noticed, in leading the attention of all men to words instead of things; for it was discovered that the language of the middle ages had been corrupt, and the primal object of every scholar became now to purify his style.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns that an excessive focus on purifying style and forms (philology) diverts intellect from higher thoughts and noble emotion: “half the intellect of the age was at once absorbed in the base sciences of grammar, logic, and rhetoric; studies utterly unworthy of the serious labor of men, and necessarily rendering those employed upon them incapable of high thoughts or noble emotion.” Evaluate writing/art by whether it privileges substantive truth and feeling over technical verbal polish alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of philological/logical/rhetorical overstudy
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the debasing tendency of philology no proof is needed beyond once reading a grammarian's notes on a great poet; logic is unnecessary for men who can reason; and about as useful to those who cannot, as a machine for forcing one foot in due succession before the other would be to a man who could not walk: while the study of rhetoric is exclusively one for men who desire to deceive or to be deceived.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage treats grammar, logic, and rhetoric as potentially corrupting when they become ends in themselves. When evaluating pedagogy, prose, or criticism, watch for signs that technical study replaces original thought, that rhetorical skill is used to obscure rather than reveal, or that analysis fragments the living power of a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination must serve truth, not fiction or pagan myth
rubrics_metrics.description: “The imagination which formerly had helped men to apprehend the truth, now tempted them to believe a falsehood. The faculties themselves wasted away in their own treason; ... the Raphael who seemed sent and inspired from heaven that he might paint Apostles and Prophets, sank at once into powerlessness at the feet of Apollo and the Muses.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic imagination should aid understanding and expression of truth (moral, religious, or social). When imagination is diverted to purely fictive or pagan subjects it weakens its capacity to convey or uphold truth. In evaluating creative work, prefer imaginative uses that illuminate deep realities rather than those that merely fabricate attractive falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique subordinate to subject and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: “In old times, men used their powers of painting to show the objects of faith; in later times, they used the objects of faith that they might show their powers of painting.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criterion demands that technical skill (colour, execution, finish) exist to serve the subject and its meaning, not as an excuse to display virtuosity while neglecting moral or narrative content. Evidence of inversion (skill for its own sake) signals artistic decline; when assessing work, check whether form serves content or content is subordinated to form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rhetorical dishonesty; favour sincere truth
rubrics_metrics.description: “The study of rhetoric is exclusively one for men who desire to deceive or to be deceived; he who has the truth at his heart need never fear the want of persuasion on his tongue.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate persuasive writing and speech for sincerity: is rhetoric employed to mask weakness or to ornament genuine conviction? Works whose persuasive techniques substitute for genuine insight are judged inferior. Prefer communication where truthfulness carries its own persuasion rather than where artifice carries the burden of belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity over nominal profession (authentic belief/practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: “This double creed, of Christianity confessed and Paganism beloved, was worse that Paganism itself, inasmuch as it refused effective and practical belief altogether.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied more generally: a surface or nominal adherence to an idea (religious, moral, aesthetic) that is contradicted by private devotion to contrary ideals is a serious fault. In evaluating characters, narratives, institutions, or cultural works, look for congruence between professed principles and lived practice; hypocrisy or split allegiance is treated as corrosive and damaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational priorities should preserve higher moral and religious studies
rubrics_metrics.description: “The entire body of the so-called Christian world has established a system of instruction for its youth, wherein neither the history of Christ's Church, nor the language of God's law, is considered a study of the smallest importance; and in which ... it is held a light matter that he should be daily guilty of lying, or debauchery, or of blasphemy, so only that he write Latin verses accurately, and with speed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging curricula, cultural training, or literary formation, prefer programs that balance technical competence with moral and historical grounding. The passage criticises an education that prizes technical facility (e.g., versification, philology) while ignoring moral character and doctrinal literacy—such imbalance contributes to cultural decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish noble grotesque from degraded jesting in art
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is jest— perpetual, careless, and not unfrequently obscene— in the most noble work of the Gothic periods; and it becomes, therefore, of the greatest possible importance to examine into the nature and essence of the Grotesque itself, and to ascertain in what respect it is that the jesting of art in its highest flight, differs from its jesting in its utmost degradation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text proposes a diagnostic for grotesque elements: some jesting or grotesque features can be elevated (noble) while others are base and obscene. Evaluate grotesque features by their intention, craftsmanship, context, and moral effect—whether they enrich and humanize the work or devolve into brutal mockery and sensual degradation (as in the 'Grotesque Renaissance' architecture criticised as perpetuating ribaldries of drunkenness).
